title: Per-model Compute Credit Mapping & Invoice Transparency PRD
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Introduce a deterministic mapping from model variant + deployment type to billable compute credits and expose transparent invoice line items so customers can reconcile costs per model, per deployment, and per-region.
background: Customers running both Hosted and Dedicated instances increasingly ask for visibility and predictability: which model inference contributed to which line item on the invoice, how quantized / small variants map to compute credits, and how Dedicated reserved capacity consumption shows up alongside per-call Hosted charges. Current invoices group charges by product bucket (hosted/dedicated) which prevents customers from attributing cost changes to model upgrades, rollout policies, or batching configuration changes.
goals: Define a stable compute-credit unit and a deterministic mapping table from model family + quantization + deployment type to compute credits per 1K tokens
Show per-model line items on invoices with attribution to deployment ID, region, and plan entitlement
Ensure backward-compatible billing for existing customers during rollout and provide a migration window and reconciliation report
Add API endpoints and Console UI views for model-level cost breakdowns for the last billing period and real-time estimated spend
non_goals: Changing base prices or plan dollar rates as part of this feature
Automatic customer-facing price changes without explicit contractual amendments
Implementing per-token dynamic pricing (this is out of scope for Q2)
requirements: R1: Define compute credit (CC) as a single unit representing 1 GPU-millisecond normalized across instance classes. Publish formula used for normalization.

R2: For each model variant in the catalog, produce a CC-per-1K-token mapping for both 1) Hosted, 2) Dedicated reserved, and 3) Dedicated burst consumption. Mapping must include quantized variants (e.g., 4-bit, 8-bit) and small-footprint models.
R3: Invoicing must surface line items that include: model SKU, deployment ID, deployment type (hosted/dedicated), region, token buckets consumed, CC consumed, unit CC price, and total amount.
R4: Add a reconciliation report that shows delta against legacy invoice grouping for the previous 6 months for customers who opt into early migration.
R5: Console: add a "Model Cost Explorer" that supports filtering by date range, model family, deployment, and region, and exports CSV with the fields in R3.
R6: Public API: GET /billing/model-usage?start=...&end=... returns CSV or JSON lines with fields in R3 and an estimated nightly cost projection header.

R7: Migration policy: customers on existing legacy aggregates can opt-in; opt-in triggers a one-billing-cycle preview and a reconciliation credit if billed more under new scheme within first two months.
R8: All mappings and formulas must be stored in a versioned catalog (human-readable) and surfaced in the Console and API with the catalog version referenced on the invoice.
R9: Support anomalies: if a model is not in the catalog at bill time, fallback mapping should apply a conservative CC multiplier and surface a 'catalog-missing' flag on the invoice for manual review.
R10: Logs and audit: every invoice must include a checksum/reference to the compute-credit catalog version and the matching usage snapshot ID for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Billing system generates invoice test artifacts for 3 sample customers that include per-model line items matching the mapping table and totals reconcile to legacy totals within +/- 1% for synthetic workloads
AC2: Console Model Cost Explorer renders model-level hourly breakdowns for a 30-day window and CSV export matches API output for the same window
AC3: Public API returns model-level usage with a header referencing compute-credit catalog version and nightly cost projection; API contract documented in OpenAPI

AC4: Migration opt-in flow available in Console; first-preview billing shows side-by-side legacy vs per-model charges and triggers a reconciliation credit if net increase > 0 within two billing cycles
AC5: Finance validates 3-month financial forecast when applying CC mapping for active enterprise customers with reserved Dedicated commits and signs off on go/no-go
AC6: If a model is absent from catalog at invoice run, line item is generated with 'catalog-missing' flag and automated ticket created in Billing queue; test covers this scenario
AC7: Unit and integration tests cover edge cases (zero token usage, negative adjustments, bursts crossing billing windows) and pass in CI
AC8: Observability: billing pipeline emits metrics for catalog lookup failures, per-model aggregation latency, and invoice generation time with defined alert thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal): Implement compute-credit catalog, mapping tool, and unit tests; generate internal preview invoices for internal customers and finance for two weeks
Phase 2 (Beta Customers): Offer opt-in to 10 enterprise customers with high Dedicated usage; collect reconciliation feedback and adjust mapping constants
Phase 3 (General Availability): Default invoice format includes per-model line items; provide migration docs and self-serve opt-in toggle for legacy customers for one billing cycle of overlap
Phase 4 (Post-GA): Monitor disputes and provide automated reconciliation credits and a 90-day reporting dashboard for migrated customers
analytics_and_metrics: Monthly Active Customers using per-model invoices
% of invoices referencing compute-credit catalog version
Average time to generate per-model invoice compared to legacy
Rate of catalog fallback (catalog-missing) per billing run
Number of billing disputes related to model attribution
Revenue delta attributable to mapping changes (simulated vs actual)
open_questions: Q1: What normalization baseline should we use for CC across differing GPU generations (A100 vs H100 vs upcoming options)? Should we weight by p99 latency or throughput?
Q2: For Dedicated reserved capacity, should CC consumption be billed against committed units first then against overage at a different unit price?
Q3: Does Finance require separate VAT treatment for per-model line items in EU invoices?
Q4: How to present model upgrades during a billing period (e.g., customer rolls from model-v1 to model-v2 mid-cycle)? Should we prorate CC mapping or use per-call attribution?
Q5: Do we provide historical mapping snapshots in API for customers to replay past invoices exactly?
decisions: D1: Use GPU-millisecond normalized baseline anchored to H100 as reference; weights for older GPUs will be a multiplier stored in catalog
D2: Bill Dedicated reservation consumption against committed CC at the customer's reserved rate first, then against overage pricing buckets
D3: Expose catalog version on invoices and in API; provide downloadable catalog CSV for audit
D4: Mid-cycle model upgrades will be billed by per-call attribution (each call stamped to model version at runtime)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers dispute changes leading to AR churn. Mitigation: Offer opt-in preview window and automated reconciliation credits for first two months
Risk: Mapping errors could materially shift revenue recognition. Mitigation: Finance sign-off and synthetic workload validation prior to GA
Risk: Performance overhead in billing pipeline due to per-call attribution. Mitigation: Batch attribution at hourly windows with pre-aggregation and caching
